review.summary: Mercedes are 1st in the Formula 1 constructors' standings on 630 points after 19 rounds, with 12 wins and 24 podiums. Andrea Kimi Antonelli is their best-placed driver, 1st overall.

review.summary: Ferrari are 2nd in the Formula 1 constructors' standings on 504 points after 19 rounds, with 2 wins and 13 podiums. Lewis Hamilton is their best-placed driver, 3rd overall.
review.lastRace: At the Mexico City Grand Prix, Lewis Hamilton finished 2nd from 1st on the grid; Charles Leclerc finished 4th from 3rd on the grid.

review.summary: Red Bull are 3rd in the Formula 1 constructors' standings on 382 points after 19 rounds, with 3 wins and 13 podiums. Max Verstappen is their best-placed driver, 2nd overall.

review.summary: McLaren are 4th in the Formula 1 constructors' standings on 365 points after 19 rounds, with 2 wins and 7 podiums. Lando Norris is their best-placed driver, 6th overall.

review.summary: Audi are 8th in the Formula 1 constructors' standings on 27 points after 19 rounds. Gabriel Bortoleto is their best-placed driver, 14th overall.

review.summary: Williams are 9th in the Formula 1 constructors' standings on 12 points after 19 rounds. Carlos Sainz is their best-placed driver, 18th overall.
review.lastRace: At the Mexico City Grand Prix, Alexander Albon finished 11th from 16th on the grid; Carlos Sainz finished 12th from 15th on the grid.

review.summary: Aston Martin are 10th in the Formula 1 constructors' standings on 7 points after 19 rounds. Fernando Alonso is their best-placed driver, 17th overall.
review.lastRace: At the Mexico City Grand Prix, Lance Stroll did not finish (Retired); Fernando Alonso did not finish (Retired).

review.lastRace: At the Mexico City Grand Prix, Sergio Pérez finished 16th from 20th on the grid; Valtteri Bottas did not finish (Retired).

review.summary: Ducati lead after eighteen rounds with eight wins and fifteen podiums, though their championship points total is not shown. Their riders are spread across the standings: Marc Marquez tops the field on 411, ahead of Fabio Di Giannantonio (274) and Alex Marquez (197), while Francesco Bagnaia sits ninth on 173 and Franco Morbidelli sixteenth on 65.
review.lastRace: At the Grand Prix of Malaysia, round eighteen, Marc Marquez won and took 25 points, with Alex Marquez third (16) and Fabio Di Giannantonio eighth (8). Franco Morbidelli finished tenth for six points, Francesco Bagnaia thirteenth (3) and Iker Lecuona fifteenth (1).

review.summary: Aprilia are second after eighteen rounds with eight wins and thirty-one podiums, though their points figure is absent. Jorge Martin tops the group on 362, with Marco Bezzecchi third overall on 332, Ai Ogura fifth (281) and Raul Fernandez seventh (242), while Lorenzo Savadori has yet to score.
review.lastRace: At the Grand Prix of Malaysia round eighteen, Ai Ogura finished fourth to take 13 points, with Marco Bezzecchi sixth (10).

review.summary: KTM are third after eighteen rounds with two wins and eight podiums, though their points total is not shown. Pedro Acosta leads the squad on 299 from fourth overall, well clear of Enea Bastianini tenth (136) and Brad Binder twelfth (118), with Maverick Viñales, Pol Espargaro and Jonas Folger far down the order.
review.lastRace: At the Grand Prix of Malaysia round eighteen, Pedro Acosta was second and took 20 points, Enea Bastianini fifth (11) and Brad Binder ninth (7). Maverick Viñales finished fourteenth for two points.

review.summary: Honda sit fourth after eighteen rounds with no wins and no podiums, though their points figure is absent. Luca Marini leads the team on 117 from thirteenth overall, ahead of Diogo Moreira (78) and Johann Zarco (56), while Joan Mir (33) and the rest trail well behind.
review.lastRace: At the Grand Prix of Malaysia round eighteen, Luca Marini finished seventh to take nine points. Johann Zarco, Diogo Moreira and Joan Mir all failed to finish, taking no points.

review.summary: Yamaha are fifth after eighteen rounds with no wins and no podiums, though their points total is not shown. Fabio Quartararo leads the squad on 79 from fourteenth overall, ahead of Jack Miller (31) and Alex Rins (29), with Toprak Razgatlioglu (18) and Augusto Fernandez (6) far behind.
review.lastRace: At the Grand Prix of Malaysia round eighteen, Fabio Quartararo finished eleventh for five points and Alex Rins twelfth (4). Jack Miller completed the race sixteenth but scored nothing, while Augusto Fernandez failed to finish.

review.summary: Jaguar lead the championship with 288 points after 17 rounds, four wins and ten podiums. Evans tops their tally at 160 and third in the standings, while Da Costa holds sixth on 128. The pair have kept the title fight close across a full calendar.
review.lastRace: At the London E-Prix, Evans recovered to fourth from fifth on the grid for 12 points, while Da Costa slipped to fifteenth from ninth and failed to score.

review.summary: Porsche sit second with 271 points, four wins and eight podiums after 17 rounds. Wehrlein leads their drivers on 169, nine clear of Müller on 102 in ninth, though the gap to Jaguar remains telling.
review.lastRace: In London both Porsche cars faded from strong grid slots. Müller dropped to twelfth from fourth and Wehrlein fell to fourteenth from third; neither scored points.

review.summary: Mahindra are third with 252 points, two wins and seven podiums. Mortara leads the pair on 137 in fifth, with De Vries close behind on 115 in seventh; their drivers have been consistently near the front.
review.lastRace: A superb London result for Mahindra. Starting first and second, De Vries finished second for 21 points and Mortara took a podium in third for 15.

review.summary: Andretti hold fourth with 229 points, two wins and seven podiums after 17 rounds. Dennis is their standout on 164 and second in the standings, while Drugovich sits fourteenth on 65 — a clear gap between the two.
review.lastRace: A poor London outing for Andretti. Drugovich finished thirteenth from eleventh and Dennis slipped to eighteenth from sixteenth; neither reached the points board.

review.summary: Citroën are fifth with 182 points, one win and six podiums. Cassidy leads the team on 114 in eighth, ahead of Vergne on 68 in twelfth. They have scored steadily but sit well clear of the leading three.
review.lastRace: A solid London double for Citroën. Cassidy finished sixth from seventh for eight points, while Vergne took seventh from twelfth and six points.

review.summary: Nissan sit sixth with 157 points, one win and six podiums after 17 rounds. Rowland is comfortably their lead driver on 137 in fourth, while Nato struggles in nineteenth on just 20; results have come largely through Rowland.
review.lastRace: In London both Nissan cars gained a little. Rowland climbed to ninth from seventeenth for three points, and Nato took tenth from nineteenth for one.

review.summary: Envision are seventh with 152 points and no wins this season, though they have taken two podiums. Buemi leads on 97 in tenth, ahead of Eriksson on 55 in sixteenth; their points have trickled through rather than from victories.
review.lastRace: At London, Buemi recovered to fifth from tenth for ten points, while Eriksson failed to finish from fifteenth on the grid and scored nothing.

review.summary: Cupra Kiro sit eighth with 128 points, one win and three podiums after 17 rounds. Martí edges his teammate on 66 in thirteenth, with Ticktum close behind on 62 in fifteenth — a genuinely even pairing.
review.lastRace: In London, Martí gained ground to finish eighth from thirteenth for four points, while Ticktum fell back to sixteenth despite starting eighth and scored nothing.

review.summary: DS Penske are ninth with 91 points, one win and a single podium after 17 rounds. Barnard leads on 68 in eleventh, well ahead of Günther on 23 in eighteenth; their season has been modest apart from Barnard's recent victory.
review.lastRace: A breakthrough London win for DS Penske. Barnard climbed to first from sixth for 25 points, while Günther finished eleventh from fourteenth and failed to score.

review.summary: Marc Marquez won the Grand Prix of Malaysia for Ducati Lenovo Team, taking 25 points from Pedro Acosta of Red Bull KTM Factory Racing (20) and Alex Marquez of BK8 Gresini Racing (16). Ai Ogura and Enea Bastianini completed the leading group. Johann Zarco, Diogo Moreira, Joan Mir and Augusto Fernandez all failed to finish.
highlights: Marc Marquez won the Grand Prix of Malaysia for Ducati Lenovo Team, taking 25 points.
Pedro Acosta finished second for Red Bull KTM Factory Racing on 20 points, with Alex Marquez third for BK8 Gresini Racing.
Johann Zarco, Diogo Moreira, Joan Mir and Augusto Fernandez all failed to finish the race.

review.summary: The winner for DS Penske was Taylor Barnard, climbing from sixth on the grid to cross first, ahead of Mahindra's Nyck De Vries (second, from pole) and team-mate Edoardo Mortara (third, from second). Buemi fifth from tenth and Cassidy sixth show a midfield that held its line. The classification also shows front-row cars falling away: Pascal Wehrlein slipped to fourteenth from third, while Joel Eriksson and Lucas Di Grassi both failed to finish.
highlights: Oliver Rowland made the biggest climb of the day, rising eight places from seventeenth to ninth for three points for Nissan.
Taylor Barnard won for DS Penske, climbing from sixth on the grid to cross the line first.
Sébastien Buemi recovered from tenth to finish fifth for Envision, taking ten points.
Joel Eriksson failed to finish from fifteenth, and Lucas Di Grassi also did not complete the race from twentieth.
